record.original_question: Can one collapse the moduli space of Einstein metrics in a natural way so that it has only finitely many connected components?

evidence.quote: Question 3.7. Can one collapse the moduli space of the Einstein metrics in a reasonable way so that there are only a finite number of components?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact manifold of dimension $n \geq 4$. An Einstein metric on $M$ is a Riemannian metric $g$ satisfying $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = \lambda g$ for some constant $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$. Let $\mathcal{E}(M)$ denote the moduli space of Einstein metrics on $M$, defined as the set of Einstein metrics modulo the action of the diffeomorphism group and rescaling. In general, $\mathcal{E}(M)$ may have infinitely many connected components.

Question: Does there exist a natural geometric procedure (a "collapsing" or quotient construction reflecting degenerations such as bubbling, orbifold limits, or volume collapse with bounded curvature) that produces from $\mathcal{E}(M)$ a topological space with only finitely many connected components, in a way that is compatible with the geometry of Einstein metrics?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys (e.g., 2025 surveys on Einstein metrics, their moduli spaces and stability) and standard references on Einstein 4-manifolds continue to discuss the finiteness of components of moduli spaces of Einstein metrics as an unresolved structural question. Related finiteness conjectures (e.g., for invariant Einstein metrics on a fixed homogeneous space) remain active open problems, and no general natural compactification reducing $\mathcal{E}(M)$ to finitely many components is known.

status_evidence.title: Einstein metrics, their moduli spaces and stability
status_evidence.snippet: Recent survey discussing the structure of moduli spaces of Einstein metrics and outstanding open questions about their global topology.
status_evidence.claim: Finiteness/structure questions about Einstein moduli spaces remain active research topics.

status_evidence.title: A Survey of Einstein Metrics on 4-Manifolds (M. T. Anderson)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describing the moduli space of Einstein metrics on 4-manifolds, including compactification questions and component structure.
status_evidence.claim: The component structure and natural compactifications of Einstein moduli spaces are discussed as open structural questions.
